title: Aleph Source Registry
description: The registry of sources Aleph may retrieve from. It is a description of what each source IS - what kind of body publishes it, under whose ownership, in what jurisdiction, at what URLs, under what crawl rules - and deliberately not an assessment of how much any source should be believed. There is NO credibility score, NO bias rating and NO political-leaning field anywhere in this schema, and additionalProperties is false so one cannot be added by accident. That absence is the design: a numeric trust weight attached to an outlet would let institutional standing substitute for evidence, and would quietly turn every downstream verdict into a judgement about who was speaking rather than about what is the case. What the registry does carry is 'evidence_tier' (what kind of artefact this source produces, and therefore what it can establish) and 'typical_independence' (whether it usually originates reporting or republishes it), both of which describe evidential structure rather than merit. 'ownership_note' is factual and public-record only - who owns or funds the outlet - so a reader can see a possible interest for themselves; Aleph never converts it into a score. The file is fully jurisdiction-parameterised: no jurisdiction, language or institution is privileged by the schema, and adding a country means adding data, not code.

registry_version.description: Version label for this registry snapshot, so a retrieval run can be reproduced against the source list it actually used.

default_rate_limit.description: Fallback politeness settings for entries that do not state their own.

jurisdiction.description: Where the source operates. Free parameters: library code must never branch on a particular jurisdiction.

code.description: Short machine code where one exists (e.g. an ISO 3166 code).

feed.description: One machine-readable entry point for a source. Feeds are listed separately from base_url because polling a declared feed is both more complete and less intrusive than crawling a site, and because a source with no feed must be handled - and reported - differently.

label.description: What this feed covers, e.g. 'economy section', 'official gazette daily index'.

language.description: BCP-47 tag, when the feed is language-specific.

topic_hint.description: Subject area the feed is scoped to. A hint for routing queries, not a filter on what may be collected.

auth_required.description: True when the feed needs credentials. Credentials themselves are NEVER stored in this file or in any shipped artefact; they come from the environment at run time.

robots_policy.description: How Aleph must behave towards this host. Recorded per source so that compliance is a property of the data, not of whoever wrote the fetcher.

respect_robots.description: Must be true in normal operation. A false value is only meaningful for a source that has granted explicit written permission, and that permission belongs in 'notes'.

crawl_allowed.description: Last observed outcome of the robots check. Null means not yet checked - which is not the same as permitted.

user_agent.description: Identifying user agent Aleph presents to this host.

rate_limit.description: Politeness budget for this source. Conservative defaults are preferred: a registry entry that gets Aleph blocked removes a source from every future analysis.

source_entry.description: One retrievable source. Every field here answers 'what is this thing and how do we reach it', never 'how much is it worth'.

kind.description: What sort of organisation publishes this. Determines which generated queries are routed here and which evidence gaps the source can close - a statistics agency and a news outlet answer different questions, and neither is a substitute for the other.

evidence_tier.description: The kind of artefact this source typically produces, which constrains what it can establish. NOT a ranking: a legislative record settles what was formally recorded but not whether a projection will hold, and a journalism item is strong evidence of what was said and weak evidence of what is true.

ownership_note.description: Factual, public-record statement of ownership or funding, e.g. 'owned by a listed media group' or 'funded by member subscriptions'. Nullable, and null means unknown rather than independent. This is disclosure for the reader to weigh; Aleph MUST NOT convert it into a trust score or use it to weight a verdict.

typical_independence.description: Whether this source usually originates its own reporting or republishes others'. Structural, not evaluative: it exists so that ten outlets carrying one wire story are counted as one observation rather than ten corroborations.

enabled.description: Whether Aleph may retrieve from this source. Disabling is an operational decision (broken feed, blocked, out of scope) and must never be used to exclude a viewpoint.

topics.description: Subject areas the source covers, for query routing.

paywall.description: Access barrier. Operationally important: an unreachable source is a coverage gap that readiness must report rather than absorb.

last_verified_at.description: When the entry's URLs and feeds were last confirmed to work.

notes.description: Operational notes only: feed quirks, encoding issues, granted permissions. Not commentary on the source's content or standing.

source_entry.$comment: The 'not' clause below is a redundant but deliberate guard: additionalProperties already rejects unknown fields, and this makes the prohibition on trust/bias scoring explicit and self-documenting to anyone extending the registry.
